finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined to the root directory with no containment check, so `../` sequences escape /srv/files and read arbitrary files the process can access.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the file contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken directly from the attacker-controlled query string
filepath.Join cleans the path, which resolves `..` segments and lets the result leave /srv/files; the result is passed to os.ReadFile
file contents returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: There is no prefix check, no filepath.Rel check, no rejection of `..`, and no auth middleware on the /dl handler at files.go:32. filepath.Join only cleans the path and does not confine it. Example request: /dl?f=../../etc/passwd reads /etc/passwd. By contrast, avatar() at files.go:22 applies filepath.Base, which does confine the path.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the unvalidated `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name), which only cleans `..` segments and does not confine the result to /srv/files; os.ReadFile reads it and files.go:18 writes it to the response. The /dl handler is registered at files.go:32 with no auth or middleware, so an anonymous attacker can request /dl?f=../../etc/passwd.
